## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Chinese translation of the *Dharmapada* — the celebrated Buddhist gnomic-verse anthology, here in [法救](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%95%91) Dharmatrāta's compilation. Translated jointly by [維祇難](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%B6%AD%E7%A5%87%E9%9B%A3) Vighna, [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) Zhī Qiān, and [竺將炎](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AB%BA%E5%B0%87%E7%82%8E) Zhú Jiāngyán in the Wú c. 224 CE. Signature: 「尊者法救撰／吳天竺沙門維祇難等譯」. The work opens with a famous preface explicating the *Dharmapada*'s origin and translation method (preserved separately in the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* but conceptually linked).

The chapters open with the *Anityā-vagga* (無常品 *Wúcháng pǐn*, "Impermanence-chapter"), in 21 verses; the chapter-titles match the *Udānavarga* Sanskrit recension rather than the Pāli *Dhammapada*'s 26 chapters.

**Abstract**

T210 is the canonical Chinese *Dharmapada* — one of the foundational texts of the East-Asian Buddhist gnomic-verse tradition. The Indic source is the Sarvāstivādin *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* recension attributed to [法救](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%95%91) Dharmatrāta, distinct from the Pāli *Dhammapada* in selection, ordering, and number of verses (T210 contains some 760 verses across 39 chapters; the Pāli has 423 across 26).

The Chinese translation is dated by the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* to *Huángwǔ* 3 (224 CE) at Wǔchāng 武昌. The famous translator's preface — recording the difficulty of Indic-Chinese translation, the collaboration of three translators, and Zhī Qiān's careful approach to verse-rendering — is one of the foundational documents of pre-modern Chinese Buddhist translation theory.

T210 was widely received in East-Asian Buddhism and is the textual basis of the *Dharmapada*-citation tradition in Chinese Buddhist commentarial literature. The companion *Dharmapada* in Chinese — *[Fǎjí yàosòng jīng (T213)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0070)* — is the late-tenth-century re-translation of the *Udānavarga* by [天息災](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E6%81%AF%E7%81%BD) Tiānxīzāi.
